question.problem: The inverse of the function $f(x)=-{3}^{4x}$ is ${f}^{-1}(x)=${{field-1}}.
question.worked_solution:
To find ${f}^{-1}(x),$ we start by replacing $f(x)$ with $y:$

$$
\begin{aligned}y & =-{3}^{4x}\end{aligned}
$$

Now, interchanging $x$ and $y$ gives

$$
\begin{aligned}x & =-{3}^{4y}.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we make $y$ the subject of the equation as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}x & =-{3}^{4y} \\ -x & ={3}^{4y} \\ {log}_{3}⁡(-x) & ={log}_{3}⁡({3}^{4y}) \\ {log}_{3}⁡(-x) & =4y \\ 4y & ={log}_{3}⁡(-x) \\ y & =\frac{{log}_{3}⁡(-x)}{4}\end{aligned}
$$

    

Therefore, the inverse function is ${f}^{-1}(x)=\frac{{log}_{3}⁡(-x)}{4}.$
